Selected work

A continuous improvement loop that runs itself

The problem
Improvement work was happening. Ownership, evidence, and reuse were not connected to it.
What I built
DRIPS: a five-stage operating loop wired across intake, execution, and evidence. No new standing meetings.
The result
A repeatable model with proof attached to every stage, designed for any team to adopt.

One front door for incoming work

The problem
Requests arrived from every direction. Routing, ownership, and status lived in people's heads.
What I built
A service blueprint: categorized intake, decision logic, named owners, visible handoffs.
The result
Leaders could see the pipeline. Delivery teams could trust it.

Evidence you can actually audit

The problem
Compliance reporting mixed stale sync records in with genuine failures. The number looked fine and meant nothing.
What I built
A classification standard that separates missing data from true failures, plus the runbook to reproduce it.
The result
A baseline leadership can defend in a room, not just present in one.

How I work

Detect what is real. Prove what changed. Leave something reusable.

Detect Root cause Improve Prove Share

Each platform gets one deliberate job. Jira executes. SharePoint holds the evidence. Teams coordinates. AI accelerates drafting and synthesis, with a human accountable for every decision that ships.

The skill is not using AI. It is knowing which tool belongs where, what it should be given, and what it should produce.

How I got here

I started in social work.

Years of sitting with people, learning how systems fail them, and finding the way through anyway.

I came into enterprise technology through an apprenticeship, not a computer science degree.

That turned out to be the advantage.

I can translate a platform into plain language, because I had to learn it that way myself. I notice adoption problems early, because I have spent my career watching what happens when a system ignores the person using it.
